name: Sandor Ellix Katz
description: Author and educator whose work explores traditional fermentation techniques, history, culture, and microbial processes across a wide range of foods and beverages.

name: Kirsten and Christopher Shockey / FermentWorks
description: Practical authors and educators covering fermented vegetables, vinegar, cider, koji, miso, tempeh, and other home-scale fermentation traditions.

name: Pascal Baudar / Wild Food Lab
description: Educator and author specializing in wild foods, indigenous microbes, terroir, and experimental fermentation using foraged ingredients.

name: Wolfe Lab at Tufts University
description: Benjamin Wolfe's microbial-ecology laboratory studies the communities that form fermented foods including cheese, sourdough, and kimchi.

name: MicrobialFoods.org
description: Science-focused project explaining fermented-food microbes, research, producers, and the microbial ecology behind fermentation.

name: National Center for Home Food Preservation
description: USDA-supported source of current, research-based home food preservation recommendations, including tested fermentation guidance.

name: NC State Extension Fermentation Resources
description: Research-based home fermentation, food-safety, and troubleshooting guidance from a university extension program.

name: Puratos Sourdough Library
description: A scientific and cultural collection preserving and analyzing sourdough cultures from around the world, with an accessible virtual library.

name: American Cheese Society
description: Professional organization offering education, resources, standards, and community for artisan cheesemakers and cheese professionals.

name: American Cheese Society Body of Knowledge
description: Technical framework covering milk microbiology, chemistry, cheesemaking, ripening, sensory evaluation, safety, and operations.

name: Charlie Bamforth / Brewing & Beer
description: Academic brewing scientist and educator whose work explains brewing chemistry, process control, quality, flavor, and beer stability.

name: John Palmer / How to Brew
description: Technically rigorous and approachable brewing reference covering ingredients, process, water chemistry, yeast, recipe design, and troubleshooting.

name: American Homebrewers Association
description: Membership organization with a substantial educational library for homebrewing beer, mead, and cider and an active practitioner community.

name: Milk The Funk Wiki
description: Evidence-driven community knowledge base for Brettanomyces, lactic-acid bacteria, mixed cultures, spontaneous fermentation, and alternative brewing microbes.

name: UC Davis Viticulture and Enology
description: Major academic center for grape growing and wine science, with research and industry resources on fermentation, chemistry, sensory science, and production.

name: UC Davis Wine Fermentation Management Guide
description: Technical guidance on wine microorganisms, yeast nutrition, temperature, pH, oxygen, sanitation, and sluggish or stuck fermentations.

name: Cornell Enology Extension
description: Research and extension material on wine fermentation, acidity, sanitation, yeast, malolactic fermentation, and cool-climate winemaking.

name: Ken Schramm / Schramm's Mead
description: Influential modern meadmaker, educator, competition co-founder, and author of a foundational practical reference on meadmaking.

name: Andrew Lea / Wittenham Hill Cider Portal
description: Technical cider resource from a fermentation scientist covering cider chemistry, microbiology, apple processing, production, and troubleshooting.

name: Hannah Crum / Kombucha Kamp
description: Longtime kombucha educator and industry consultant offering extensive practical material for home and commercial kombucha brewing.

name: Jeremy Umansky and Rich Shih / Koji Alchemy
description: Practical English-language authority on culinary koji and its application to amino sauces, miso, charcuterie, vegetables, and other foods.

name: World Institute of Kimchi
description: South Korean government research institute devoted to kimchi fermentation, microbial resources, safety, health, production, storage, and culture.

name: National Research Institute of Brewing (Japan)
description: Japan's national alcoholic-beverage research institute and an authoritative English-language source on sake, koji, yeast, shochu, and brewing science.

name: NRIB: What Is Koji?
description: Accessible scientific introduction to yellow, black, and white koji molds and their roles in sake, shochu, miso, soy sauce, and vinegar.

name: Jyoti Prakash Tamang / Ethno-microbiology of Ethnic Indian Fermented Foods
description: Scholarly work documenting the microbiology and indigenous knowledge of fermented vegetables, soybeans, cereals, dairy, meats, and beverages across India and the Himalayas.

name: Buddhiman Tamang / Sikkim University
description: Food microbiologist specializing in lactic-acid bacteria, functional foods, and fermentation and biopreservation of traditional Himalayan vegetable products.

name: Oluwafemi Adebo / University of Johannesburg
description: Food scientist researching indigenous African foods, fermentation, metabolomics, starter cultures, and improvement of traditional food processes.

name: Mary Obodai / CSIR College of Science and Technology
description: Ghanaian food microbiologist with decades of research experience, including specialization in the microbiota of African fermented foods.

name: African Fermented Food Microbiome Project
description: Metagenomic research characterizing fermented foods from Burkina Faso, Ghana, Kenya, and Nigeria and comparing their microbial communities globally.

name: Sijmen Schoustra / Wageningen University
description: Microbial ecologist studying traditional African fermented-food ecosystems and their connections to nutrition, food security, and indigenous knowledge.

name: Hacettepe University FoodOmics Laboratory
description: English-language research site for a laboratory studying traditional fermented-food microbiota through microbiology, sequencing, metagenomics, and foodomics.

name: Traditional Fermented Foods in Anatolia
description: English open-access overview of Anatolian yogurt, ayran, kefir, kurut, cheese, tarhana, boza, pickles, şalgam, vinegar, wine, and sucuk.

name: Traditional Fermented Foods and Beverages in Iraq
description: Open-access English scholarly resource documenting preparation of Iraqi basturma, smoked liban, Aushari cheese, turshi, sour khobz, and traditional beverages.

name: Traditional Fermented Milk Products of the Eastern Mediterranean
description: Scientific review of traditional fermented milks, their production processes, microbial populations, sensory characteristics, safety, and cultural significance.

name: Persian Kashk Zard Fermentation Study
description: Open-access investigation of Iran's traditional fermented yogurt-and-wheat product kashk zard, including its two-stage process and microbial community.

name: FAO: Cereal Fermentations in Latin America
description: English reference covering fermented maize foods and beverages across Latin America, including chicha, atole agrio, cachiri, pozol, and related traditions.

name: Rosane Freitas Schwan / Federal University of Lavras
description: Brazilian fermentation microbiologist whose group has studied cocoa, coffee, cassava, sugarcane, defined starter cultures, and tropical fermentations for decades.

name: Indigenous Latin American Fermented Foods
description: English scientific overview of indigenous fermentation involving cereals, tubers, fruits, and vegetables, including spontaneous communities and starter-culture research.

name: FAO: Fermented Fruits and Vegetables — A Global Perspective
description: Broad English practical and cultural reference covering indigenous fruit and vegetable fermentation across Africa, Asia, and Latin America.

name: Ethnic Fermented Foods of the World
description: Modern open-access global overview of traditional fermentation technologies and foods, organized geographically and by fermentation mechanism.

name: Sandor Katz / Sandorkraut YouTube Channel
description: Sandor Katz's channel features demonstrations, lectures, interviews, travel, and discussions of fermentation as technique, preservation practice, culture, and social history.

name: UC Food Safety / EATLAC Science of Fermentation
description: University-led video collection covering fruit and vegetable fermentation science, food safety, health claims, practical production, and troubleshooting.

name: Escarpment Labs YouTube Channel
description: Technical brewing-microbiology webinars covering yeast health, pitch rates, fermentation performance, contamination, mixed cultures, kveik, Brettanomyces, flavor compounds, and troubleshooting.

name: Master Brewers Association Video Resources
description: Professional brewing education covering science, technology, history, quality control, ingredients, fermentation, brewery operations, and troubleshooting.

name: Brewers Association Video Archive
description: Professional brewing presentations and laboratory demonstrations, including standardized methods for yeast counting, pH, apparent extract, aseptic sampling, and spoilage-organism detection.

name: Australian Wine Research Institute Webinar Archive
description: Technical wine-science webinars on yeast, malolactic fermentation, stuck fermentation, Brettanomyces, reductive aromas, extraction, sanitation, smoke taint, and sensory science.

name: The Sourdough Journey
description: Experiment-driven sourdough instruction comparing temperature, inoculation, percentage rise, starter condition, timing, shaping, and crumb structure through controlled bakes.

name: The Bread Code
description: Engineering-oriented explanations of sourdough history, enzymes, gluten, wild yeast, lactic-acid bacteria, fermentation variables, diagnostics, and adaptable bread technique.

name: ChainBaker
description: Systematic bread demonstrations showing how fermentation time, temperature, inoculation, hydration, salt, kneading, flour, preferments, and process order affect dough.

name: Center for Dairy Research — University of Wisconsin–Madison Videos
description: University dairy-science videos on cheesemaking, cheese chemistry, defects, processing, cultures, food safety, and commercial dairy production.

name: Harvard Science & Cooking Fermentation Lectures
description: University public lectures pairing researchers with expert practitioners to explore the scientific principles underlying fermentation and culinary technique.

name: KojiCon Video Presentations
description: Presentations from craftspeople, researchers, brewers, historians, and culinary professionals combining koji heritage, contemporary technique, and fermentation science.

name: UC Master Food Preserver Fermentation Videos
description: Curated research-based extension videos from multiple universities covering vegetable fermentation, kombucha, yogurt, and home-fermentation safety.

name: Smithsonian Food History and Indigenous Foodways Videos
description: Museum lectures and demonstrations exploring Indigenous food systems, preservation, food sovereignty, culinary history, and the cultural setting of traditional food practices.

name: K-State Rapid Response Center — Pickling and Fermentation
description: Research-based hub covering brined and fermented pickles, sauerkraut, kimchi, kombucha, fermentation vessels, troubleshooting, and tested preservation methods.

name: K-State Extension — Taking a New Look at Fermented Foods
description: Accessible extension introduction to fermented foods, microorganisms, health considerations, food safety, vegetable-fermentation methods, sauerkraut, and kimchi.

name: K-State Extension Food Safety
description: Statewide program connecting consumers and food businesses with research-based preservation guidance, specialists, instructional resources, and workshops.

name: MU Extension — Safely Fermenting Food at Home
description: Concise research-based safety guidance on salt concentration, suitable containers, temperature, sanitation, storage, and avoiding unsafe substitutions during vegetable fermentation.

name: MU Extension Food Preservation
description: Statewide Missouri program providing research-based publications, workshops, online instruction, tested recipes, newsletters, and access to preservation specialists.

name: K-State Marais des Cygnes District Food Preservation
description: Regional Miami and Linn County program offering preservation classes throughout the year and by request, tested resources, local specialists, and pressure-canner gauge testing.

name: K-State Johnson County Extension Food Preservation
description: Regional food-preservation program connecting Kansas City-area residents with research-based instruction, food-safety guidance, specialists, and trained Master Food Volunteers.
